content: Amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium, marketed as AUGMENTIN, is indicated for the treatment of infections caused by susceptible bacteria. Its use is specifically recommended to reduce the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to maintain the effectiveness of AUGMENTIN and other antibacterial drugs. AUGMENTIN should only be prescribed for infections that are either proven or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria susceptible to this combination therapy. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns should be considered to make an empiric choice of therapy. AUGMENTIN is a combination of a penicillin-class antibacterial agent and a beta-lactamase inhibitor. It is indicated for the treatment of infections caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of designated bacteria in the following conditions: 1. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: These include infections caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis. 2. Acute Bacterial Otitis Media: This condition is caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of H. influenzae and M. catarrhalis. 3. Sinusitis: Infections caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of H. influenzae and M. catarrhalis fall under this category. 4. Skin and Skin Structure Infections: These include infections caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella species. 5. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): These are caused by beta-lactamase–producing isolates of E. coli, Klebsiella species, and Enterobacter species. Limitations of Use: AUGMENTIN should not be used in cases where susceptibility testing indicates that the causative organism is sensitive to amoxicillin alone, as this suggests the absence of beta-lactamase production.
